profile.bio: Undergraduate physics student at the University of Chittagong with a passion for nuclear physics and quantum mechanics. Pursuing research at the intersection of nuclear theory and fusion technology, I aim to contribute to the development of clean, sustainable energy through advanced plasma physics and nuclear fusion science. I am seeking a scholarship to further explore fusion reactor design and computational nuclear physics.

papers.title: Reaction-Conditioned Residual-Risk Screening of 56Fe Neutron Cross-Section Predictions Using EXFOR Data
papers.abstract: Reaction-conditioned residual-risk screening applied to 17,329 reaction-harmonized EXFOR measurements of 56Fe, drawn from 135 experiment groups across five neutron-induced channels. Under nested experiment-group holdout the experiment-balanced error falls by about 12 percent while every group stays represented, a reduction that matched-random retention does not reproduce. The method is offered as an empirical diagnostic that complements evaluated libraries, covariance assessment and expert review, not as physical uncertainty quantification.
papers.authors: Mustofa Khalid Ovi, Md. Shahnewaj Al Hasan, Mst. Ummey Habiba Musfika, Md. Salman Shamil, A. K. M. Rezaur Rahman, Md. Masum Rana Pramanik
papers.venue: International Journal of Modern Physics E · Under review

papers.title: Theoretical Evaluation of Level-Density Effects in Neutron-Induced Fe(n,p)Mn Reactions
papers.abstract: Excitation functions for all four Fe(n,p)Mn reactions computed with the TALYS reaction code under four nuclear level-density models (CTFG, BSFG, GSM and HFB), then benchmarked against the EXFOR record and the TENDL-2023, JEFF-3.3, JENDL-5 and ENDF/B-VIII.1 libraries. A ratio-to-mean spread metric from 1 to 20 MeV quantifies how far the models diverge and shows a strongly isotope-dependent sensitivity to the level-density choice. For the least-measured isotopes, level density is the dominant source of theoretical uncertainty across most of the excitation function.
